v0_1_1.summary: Split the article editor into page and business components while preserving existing article assets and writing workflows.

v0_1_2.summary: Redesigned the workspace and added projects, archiving, Fork, history comparisons and editor appearance settings. Article directories can be restored after refresh. Light/dark article preview switching was not yet available.

v0_1_3.summary: Editor themes manage colors and fonts, with JSON import/export, custom combinations and migration of older appearance settings. Source coloring follows the editor theme; Rainy Studio Slate adds local fonts. Article themes and exports remain independent. The app version comes from package.json and release notes use a separate JSON file.

v0_1_3_1.summary: Separated heading and interface fonts; adapted four built-in themes, with neutral gray colors and serif headings for Mist Gray. Eyebrows use English; page headings and eyebrows share styles and specification IDs. Headings use mt-1 and adjacent descriptions use mt-3.

v0_1_4.summary: Continued improvements to templates, snippets, themes and writing. This version was in development; changes are grouped by feature.

sections.title: Templates and libraries
items: Synced built-in themes, snippets, categories and starter templates from the user's local library. Renamed the general snippet category to Default; new libraries include Default and Zixu categories, retaining icons and user edits.

Starter templates use category directories and an index for names, descriptions, order and icons. They share collapsible category panels and creation controls with snippets. Renaming migrates files and indexes; failures restore the original directory and report incomplete rollback.
Merged snippets and starter templates into the Templates page with tabs, unified navigation, URL state and redirects from old routes.
Lists and details scroll independently. Expanded categories scroll with the list; narrow screens cap list height to leave room for editing.
User snippets use category directories, with names, descriptions, order and icons in an index. Uncategorized snippets also have their own directory.
Category cards reuse collapsible panels. The edit button sits left of the count, appears on hover or keyboard focus, and its tooltip is not clipped.
Category dialogs include icon selection. Whole snippet and starter-template cards can be selected.
Both content types share a separate information dialog. Starter-template source editing hides metadata while preserving unknown fields, dates, theme bindings and comments.

Click snippet or template source to type; changes show Source editing. Cancel and Save content stay at the bottom right. Names share a row with triggers or filenames; descriptions stay in the list and information dialog.

New snippets and starter templates require a filename. Confirming information keeps a draft; the first content save writes filename, metadata and body together. Existing files can be renamed, with collision checks, original-file retention and new-file rollback on failure.

Cmd/Ctrl+S saves current snippet or template content. With an information dialog open, it saves that form without also saving the article. Read-only, unchanged, composition, saving and confirmation states retain their guards.

Existing-file information and body are saved separately. Cancelling information edits preserves the body draft, and saving information retains unsaved body edits. Both previews reuse the light/dark switch and conversion workflow.
Markdown and Tailwind utilities render live beside the source; a draggable divider adjusts widths. Invalid metadata can be repaired separately.
Preserved drafts in both tabs, departure confirmation, failed-write protection, refresh retry and directory-session isolation.

sections.title: Snippet input and keyboard controls
items: Insert element Markdown actions use one native edit and support Cmd/Ctrl+Z undo and redo. Imported-image references also enter undo history; original content remains protected on failure.
The snippet library in Insert element now has one Open snippet library action: insert // at the start of a line, adding a newline first when necessary, then open the list.
The list groups snippets by library category. Left/right expands, collapses or returns to the parent; up/down moves through categories and snippets.
Typing a trigger filters and expands matching categories. Enter or Tab inserts a snippet; Esc closes the list. Completion is suspended during input-method composition.
The keyboard-selected item scrolls into view while preserving editor scroll position and input focus.
Removed preset leading blank lines from snippets. Insertion checks line position and combines any required newline with the snippet in one undoable edit.
Cursor markers restore the insertion point. Input and highlight layers use matching line breaks; delayed cursor callbacks that could overwrite later selections were removed.

sections.title: Article themes
items: Color-use inspection now covers currentColor, transparent backgrounds and gradient sources. Node palettes read actual CSS defaults so body and code colors are not mistaken for heading colors.

Added reading hints, tinted quotations and code samples covering all 11 color tokens. Variable-based border/background shorthands are no longer falsely reported as fixed colors; actual fixed CSS colors remain locatable.

Article previews and color controls work both ways: preview popups show actual tokens and locate their controls; hovering a control highlights matching article nodes. Node overrides and fixed CSS colors retain their own provenance. Light/dark inspection is consistent, with 300ms opacity transitions.

Renamed Basic Typography to Basic and redesigned headings, body, quotes and tables for Basic, Rainy Paper, Jiangxu, Mokan and Qingyan, incrementing each theme once. Rainy Paper uses brand blue-gray and Sen; exports include layout styles needed by heading tags.
The preview toolbar shows a book icon, theme name and version. It opens a picker with themes on the left and the current article preview on the right.
Previewing and applying are separate. Returning to editing keeps the original theme; applying returns to the editor. Manuscript information uses the same picker.
Moved the light/dark switch beside the theme button and save status to the far right. File and theme information buttons share components and classes.
Added theme deletion with confirmation; deleting a library entry retains existing article snapshots. Removed eight experimental themes and added Zixu with matching snippets.
CSS/JSON validation is available after edits and validates both together. Failed tabs use danger styling; unvalidated edits show a modified marker.
Theme saving requires successful validation. Disabled saving explains Validate first, and Reset changes includes an icon.
Moved validation to the footer, enlarged code areas and added draggable column widths. Node reset buttons sit directly left of color controls.
Removed extra borders around article previews. Dark-mode theme switching updates the body snapshot and avoids blank content or duplicate navigation.

sections.title: Manuscript information and drafting
items: New article entry points share a drafting dialog with a structure menu on the left, layout preview on the right and creation controls at the bottom.
Manuscript information uses the shared dialog frame, grouping basic information, layout/ownership and management; save actions stay in the footer.
Dialog height follows content. Field cards no longer stretch with the adjacent panel; duplicate project-order buttons were removed.
Retained title, description, author, categories and project editing, plus history, deletion and unarchiving.
New drafts use new dates and the current article theme. Editing information or template bodies preserves existing metadata and body boundaries.

sections.title: Appearance and settings
items: Fixed ordinary source text staying fully opaque when inspecting headings, quotes or syntax markers. Related text remains bright; other text fades to 50% over 300ms.
Corrected source backgrounds, covered ancestor backgrounds, placeholders and derived button colors. Theme copying retains palette references; independent fields with equal HEX values are not merged.

Editor themes include color-use inspection. Hover a preview element to see its role and token, then click to locate its control. Hovering or focusing a color control keeps related preview content fully opaque and fades other branches to 50%, with smooth positioning and opacity.
Color-use popups fade out over 200ms after leaving. Passing over other preview elements delays replacement; entering the popup cancels closing and switching so its actions remain clickable.
Editor-theme previews follow the workspace display mode and system changes. Sun/moon buttons show light and dark modes; a temporary preview override remains available.

Entering the color list restores all control opacities. The editor preview covers all 33 roles, including popups, hover, progress, selection, accent, warning and danger examples; forms moved to the top right.
Settings use three tabs with a compact local-directory layout. Appearance supports live preview, cancellation and explicit saving.

The editor-theme header edits name, JSON filename ID and version. Regular renames check collisions and update saved appearance references. Changing the Basic theme ID saves a separate file. Versions still increment automatically when not edited manually.
Custom combinations use separate color and font card dialogs; the two can come from different themes.
Added Liuzi, Muxue, Yanyang and Mobai appearances. The first three retain their full-color variants as II, with consistent theme ordering.
Mobai uses black, white and gray. Color cards show an accent swatch followed by equal-width semantic colors.
Color, font and typography-node panels share components and classes; local utilities retain differences.
Selectable palette colors show HEX on hover/focus and a Tailwind name for exact matches. Current colors in the picker use the same labels; custom colors are not approximated.
Decorative eyebrows share one primitive, theme accent color and independent font field. Heading, body and source fonts have separate responsibilities.
Added local fonts and font previews with support for older theme fields. Themes appear after restoration and validation to reduce appearance flashes on refresh.
Preview selection opacity, warning text and danger-button states follow actual components. Unsaved drafts and temporary display modes are identified; color roles retain independent references.

sections.title: Preview, styles and experience fixes
items: Articles, snippets and templates share Markdown rendering and on-demand styles. Theme CSS does not load external links or scripts; safe HTML styling is retained.
Article styling is isolated in Shadow DOM so body utilities cannot alter the tool interface. Fixed cursor/highlight misalignment in long HTML.
Live preview coalesces rapid style compilation and ignores obsolete results. Switching articles or themes cleans up old preview listeners.
Image examples use Rainy Design reference artwork. Old built-in placeholder paths can also preview samples without requesting missing images.
Author/ending content uses themed closing, author and contact layouts. Horizontal scrolling shows three sample images with captions following the article theme.
Release notes use the standard close button and group current-version changes into collapsible categories.

sections.title: Article copying and format references
items: Copying retains horizontal-image dimensions, spacing, shrinking and scrolling, plus gradients, paper backgrounds and specified image attributes. Responsive dimensions use CSS Typed OM so automatic widths are not fixed to pixels.
Article copying and dark preview share RGB conversion and preserve alpha in gradients and shadows. Conversion failures appear as copy errors.

Created JSON and Markdown format references from three user-provided images, recording sources, supported items, restrictions and exceptions. Real editor verification and validator integration were left for later discussion.

New snippet, starter-template and article-theme writes are checked against the format JSON. Copying checks source structure, theme/compiled styles and output HTML. Tailwind classes are checked for permitted static conversion before removal from output. Older content remains readable; unmatched items identify locations and block writing or copying.

v0_1_5.summary: Completed component/style cleanup, named-library creation guards, and fixes to draft previews and theme copying.

sections.title: Components and styles
items: Peer top-level dialogs are mutually exclusive; specified parent/child dialogs retain their hierarchy.
Removed 39 declarations duplicating preflight defaults; retained six padding declarations that override defaults at the md breakpoint or on icon buttons.
Editor-theme variables come from one :root stylesheet in head and also apply to dialogs mounted under body.
Audited and removed unused component styles and the old article-renaming dialog. Simple one-off styles moved to their call sites to reduce duplication.

sections.title: Libraries
items: Creating a library requires a directory name before selecting a parent. Files are generated only inside the named child directory.
Existing same-name child directories are rejected with a readable explanation.
Opening a library checks its structure. Failed initialization cleans up its newly created directory only after confirming there is no other content, preventing unintended writes or deletion.

sections.title: Drafting and theme workflows
items: Draft previews use the same Markdown/Tailwind layout pipeline as article bodies and show the layout expected after creation.
Copy and apply in the article-theme library creates and opens a Fork for saved manuscripts while retaining the original. An unsaved new draft adopts the theme directly and returns to editing.

sections.title: Known limitations
items: Copying was blocked, with locations reported, when body markup such as m-0, <th> or <h4> was absent from the WeChat format list.

v0_1_6.summary: Improved article management, format checking and theme/template workflows; added statistics/export, refined local-library dialogs, and remembered line-number and ungrouped-collapse preferences globally.

sections.title: Release notes
items: Release blocks collapse to version, status and summary; inner category rows collapse with them.
Added Expand all/Collapse all for release blocks, using 200ms max-height transitions and respecting reduced motion.
Dialog sections share compact padding and footer actions, reducing layout differences between pages.

sections.title: Clipboard receiver
items: The receiver is an expandable bottom panel. Paste controls and received content appear when expanded; its surface follows article-preview light/dark mode.

sections.title: Local libraries
items: New library uses a shared dialog for naming, previewing the child location and selecting its parent before creation; the Settings page layout is retained.
Names are validated before directory selection. Cancelling the picker, collisions and write failures retain input for retry. Creation shows progress and prevents duplicate submission or closing.
Unsaved article and appearance changes are handled first. The dialog joins mutual exclusion, focuses the name field and retains keyboard focus/return behavior.

sections.title: Article management
items: Article lists support multiple selection and Select all filtered results, with clear selected states.
Unarchived articles can move to projects/Ungrouped or archive in bulk. Archived articles can be restored or deleted; deletion lists each target and asks for confirmation.
Project names open their article collections. Articles without a project are called Ungrouped.
The Ungrouped sidebar list collapses independently; its name still opens the collection.
Ungrouped collapse state is a browser-wide preference, retained across pages, libraries, refreshes and restarts, with cross-tab synchronization.
Clicking Archive again toggles its sidebar manuscripts. Hover/focus on collection names moves labels upward over 300ms to show document counts, with reduced-motion support.
Moved the new-project form beneath the sidebar Projects heading. Renamed the bulk-action destination to Group into, distinguishing projects from category tags.
Moved project pinning after the settings menu, adjusted header spacing and enlarged the new-project hit area.

sections.title: WeChat format checking
items: The format list became a tiered risk record distinguishing shorthands, longhands and alternatives; unlisted items are explicitly unverified.

Snippets and starter templates validate before saving; prohibited formats and engine failures block writes, while review notices remain visible. Copying consolidates source, rendering and output findings for the user's decision.
Results identify source/render provenance and locatable lines. Built-in snippets and article themes were revised against the current format list.
The full WeChat copy, paste, save-draft, reopen and mobile-preview workflow was tested.
Tested portions of the format list passed for the tested cases. Broader HTML/CSS compatibility and stability remained for later review.

Checks source tag structure before browser HTML repair, locating unclosed/mismatched tags, nesting, attribute quotes and content in closing tags. Errors block snippet/template writes. Code examples, escaped text, autolinks, void elements and legal omitted closing tags are handled separately.
Fixed four incorrect span closing tags and one missing h2 closing tag in the Rainy Design sample, syncing the library, project mirror and built-in templates.

Added Format check between Update styles and Save. It checks the current draft without writing the article or clipboard; its only footer action is Close. Close, Do not copy and Copy anyway use consistent icons.

sections.title: Article themes
items: Synced built-in and local article themes. Article lists, editor and theme dialogs show available updates and can adopt the latest library version.
Applying an article theme asks how to handle unsaved edits, with explicit Save, Discard and Cancel outcomes.
Dark preview uses the page surface rather than writing a light paper background into the body; fixed divider contrast in both modes.
Article themes no longer specify reader fonts; the separate font panel was removed.
All article-theme images retain automatic height, max-width 100% and block display as baseline rules.

sections.title: Editor appearance
items: Editor-theme cards use a 4×3 array of dots to show twelve semantic colors.

sections.title: Source and preview
items: Body line numbers count actual newlines rather than visual wraps. Highlight and input share font, padding and width and stay aligned when resizing columns.
Line-number visibility is globally remembered across articles, navigation and restarts, and synchronized across tabs.
Source lines with warnings/errors use different colors; hovering a line number explains the finding.
Inserting a snippet regenerates its required styles immediately, without manually clicking Update styles.
Code blocks retain line breaks; two or more consecutive blank lines remain visible as empty paragraphs in previews and output.
Article preview styles are isolated from editor appearance so tool fonts and colors cannot affect the body.

Style updates and post-save compilation summarize revision, class count and pass/warning/error totals from the same check. Styles generated is hidden for warnings/errors. The latest preview is committed before checking; delayed mounts trigger a new check and stale results cannot overwrite the current manuscript.

sections.title: Snippets and starter templates
items: Replaced automatic table-of-contents generation with an insertable built-in text snippet that authors can adjust.
Snippets have independent icons shown in the library and insertion menu; older snippets use defaults.
Starter templates also support icons. Their information dialogs and both category types share icon selection and previews.
Snippet/template cards include quick editing, and starter-template cards always show category tags.

The current article, including unsaved edits, can become a starter template. Its information dialog collects filename, category and metadata without changing the article. Local-media references explain that assets must be reimported.
Cmd/Ctrl+S validates and saves snippet, template and article-theme code in one action. Failed validation retains drafts; saving shows progress and the final result retains review notices.

Side-by-side and three-image layouts use table cells instead of prohibited div/flex/gap. Replaced built-in content with the current library's 7 article themes, 20 snippets and 5 starter templates, removing old entries while retaining categories, icons and metadata.

Merged the external library's updates for paired images, simple tables and three-image rows into built-in snippets and the project mirror. Categories, triggers, icons and templates match the current library.

sections.title: Article statistics and export
items: The editor's statistics show body characters, reading time and counts of headings, paragraphs, images, links and code blocks. The five lower counts have individual icons.
Export the current Markdown source or a ZIP containing article.md and media/ assets.
Moved Export article left of the toolbar divider beside statistics, history and template creation.
Long images and A4 PDFs use the current article theme's light preview. PDF pages contain images, so text is not selectable. Unloaded resources or browser canvas limits stop the operation explicitly.

v0_1_7.summary: Completed shared-image and asset management, bulk organization, image information, local-image diagnostics and full-article copying with mixed images; unified previews, pagination and workspace branding.

sections.title: Interface branding
items: The upper-left workspace logo uses the existing R/ SVG favicon, with background/foreground colors from the editor theme. Expanded/collapsed sidebars share it, retaining expansion controls and keyboard focus.

sections.title: Built-in library
items: Synced wording revisions in starter samples from the current library while retaining categories, metadata and other template content.

sections.title: Assets and image reuse
items: Assets distinguish shared and article images, with search, owning-article filtering, previews and details. Long filenames truncate in lists/details and show their full value on hover.
Shared images live in shared/image, created on first import rather than empty reads. Supports multiple imports, image-content identification and collision-safe naming.
Insert element includes Choose from assets. The picker identifies the target article and cursor location; adopting from Assets returns to the current article with the selection retained.

Adopted shared images become independent article copies using media/image references. Existing current-article images insert references only. Native undo/redo is supported; saving, reopening, Fork and ZIP export retain images.

Processing prevents duplicate adoption/closing; failures retain selection for retry. Results check library, manuscript and request identity to keep old operations out of new drafts. Archived articles and invalid metadata/theme snapshots remain protected.

Successful imports clear old filters/selections, and library changes reset gallery state. Images fit fully inside fixed-aspect containers. Filenames truncate at complete Unicode characters, and references encode parentheses and other symbols.

sections.title: Asset management and authoring checks
items: Unified page headers for articles, templates, themes, settings and assets, aligning action bars at the bottom. Assets omit the library description, add source icons and filter by group/article. Entry from an article selects its assets.

Source, search and browsing controls share one toolbar. Selection sits left of search; group, article, sort and layout use right-side icons. Menus are exclusive, sorting changes direction, and a remembered 1–4 slider controls layout; one column is a horizontal list. Assets and the image picker share the toolbar, with horizontal scrolling on narrow screens.

Supports bulk move/copy and confirmed deletion. Selection expands actions in place; collapse retains checks, while source/filter/search changes clear them. Unreferenced images move; referenced images copy and retain originals. Partial failures identify retryable items.

Filename and rename pencil stay adjacent; long names reserve button space. Card backgrounds use the normal cursor, while images/names/buttons use a pointer. Other background areas select details or toggle selection; interactive controls remain independent. Top-left checkboxes appear on hover/focus and remain visible for touch or selection. Download, delete, adopt and resolution/description/replacement details are retained.

Small asset buttons share one component. Regular actions are 36×36 squares; filename/description pencils have no background and sit beside text. Cards, details, toolbar and image picker share colors, corners and tooltips, including disabled explanations.

Filename/description pencils align vertically with text. Detail-image clicks or View original open a shared preview with zoom, 100% and fit controls. Arrow keys browse all images in the current sorted directory; Esc returns to the opener.

Assets and the image picker share pagination: 10, 20, 50 or 100 per page, default 20, remembered globally. Only current-page thumbnails mount. Paging retains checks; Select all targets the page, bulk actions target all checked images, and filtering/sorting/page-size changes return to page one.

Full-article rich-text copying embeds local image bytes at their original positions, retaining Markdown/HTML/repeated-image order and reading repeated images once. Read failures or unready images leave the clipboard intact. Library/article changes or newer copy requests cancel old results. Saving, styling and format checks remain; preparation no longer requests local images over HTTP.
Body checks distinguish missing local image files from temporarily unverifiable ones. They locate Markdown/HTML references and ignore code examples.

Authoring checks work independently of line numbers. Hidden numbers still show red/yellow diagnostic dots and both severities can share a line. The global error-checking switch affects live checks; save, manual and copy checks still run.
Disabled icon actions retain native disabling while exposing purpose/reason on hover or keyboard focus. Menus support keyboard navigation, Esc and focus return.
Mobile display mode shows only its current icon and opens downward on click; desktop sidebar menus continue opening upward.

Deletion/move dialogs show reference counts in the footer and list filenames once. Opening counts current-draft body references only; Scan references explicitly reads saved workspace bodies/history. One scan handles a selection, supports cancellation and reports incomplete reads for retry. Actual paths distinguish independent article copies.

v0_1_8.summary: Improved README, numbered Agent tutorials and theme documentation; added configurable static-server ports, monthly article indexes, scoped category/check management and bulk tag removal. Unified image-combination checks/copying, synced built-in resources and adopted MIT licensing.

sections.title: Documentation and tutorials
items: Rewrote the human README with an Agent Readable link, installation/startup, data/backups, FAQ and capability boundaries.
Added staged installation and three numbered AGENT-GUIDE tutorials. THEME centralizes creation rules and complete examples for editor/article themes, snippets, starter templates and full articles.

sections.title: Local startup
items: The static server supports --port and --help, defaults to 3500 and binds only to 127.0.0.1. Invalid, duplicate and unknown arguments fail before building; occupied ports do not cause existing processes to be terminated.

sections.title: Article lists and categories
items: Lists read monthly index summaries first and read source/theme snapshots only for the opened article. Old indexes can be explicitly rebuilt. Saves synchronize categories/summaries, with batched monthly index writes.

Categories follow the current group/archive scope. Multiple-tag selection and removal confirmation affect only filtered unarchived articles, retaining body, other metadata and history; partial failures are reported separately.

List checks are independent of editor state. Checking the current scope shows progress and supports cancellation, aggregating unchecked/stale/failed records by article. Results describe the last check; old tasks cannot populate a new scope.
The index scan/rebuild button uses a document/circular-arrow icon with the same tooltip and behavior.

sections.title: Image layout and format checking
items: The format list recorded the complete image combination max-width:100%, height:auto and display:block. Matching on one image rule or inline style treated automatic height as usable; isolated height stayed low priority. Shared theme/article/snippet/template checks did not combine separate rules or utilities for exemptions.
Rich-text copying retained qualifying image height:auto instead of freezing preview pixel height. Other dimension handling, sanitization and mixed-image copying followed the existing workflow.

sections.title: Local milestone and open-source preparation
items: 0.1.8 passed local acceptance, reached its local milestone, adopted MIT licensing and prepared source/static release candidates.

v0_2_0.summary: First public release: library format strategies are decoupled into external support rules, validator and formatter; WeChat defaults follow official specifications, with shared find/replace and guided initialization.

sections.title: Format strategies and validation
items: Each library binds one trio under format/. validator.rules[] and formatter.steps[] call registered capabilities. Unknown fields, parameters/capabilities, duplicate IDs and conflicts produce explicit errors.
WeChat defaults follow the official plugin specification. Removed older compatibility tiers, font exemptions and the three-image-property criterion; mp-darkmode converts an isolated copy.
JSON controls line breaks, blank lines, code whitespace/colors, preview backgrounds, conversions, retained attributes and export options; editor themes remain independent.
Live checks are separate from actual layout/dark-mode checks. Cancellation or resource/measurement failures are not passes. Duplicate notices merge, and failed rules cannot also appear as passed.
leaf/nodeleaf structure is checked before browser HTML repair, avoiding missed invalid children moved by the parser.
Library changes/reloads invalidate old tasks, styles and caches. Damaged configuration prompts repair; a wholly missing trio explicitly identifies built-in fallback.
Previews and layout checks use local static bootstrap scripts and non-executable JSON, compatible with existing static-server CSP.

sections.title: Editing and initialization
items: Article bodies, theme CSS/JSON, snippets and starter templates share find/replace, with case matching, counts, next/previous, single/all replacement and one-step undo. Read-only, composition and save guards remain.

Undo/redo for Find, Replace and source is isolated by current focus. Cmd/Ctrl+G navigates matches, Shift reverses direction, and Cmd/Ctrl+Enter in Replace replaces the current match. Replace all confirms scope/count/deletion semantics and remains one undoable action.
The Agent guide uses available question tools to choose new/existing libraries, default data/my-library or a custom path, and format configuration. Browser authorization is completed separately.

Built-in resources sync from the approved test-library inventory, retaining themes, snippets, starter templates and categories; articles/ contains no preloaded bodies, snapshots, history or monthly indexes.
The default starter-template group starts collapsed in the new-article dialog.
Refresh/library loading uses a full-screen state that fades out over 300ms with the current editor appearance.
Clipboard-receiver instructions are placeholders rather than real content, so pasting/typing does not insert help text.
The default editor appearance is Rainy Design · Slate with system-following color mode.
Line-number and Insert element actions use shared icon buttons with popup labels, retaining visibility state and native menu behavior.

Source highlighting and native input share one scroll container, removing scrollTop catch-up between text layers. Cursor visibility, find navigation and post-insertion scrolling use that same viewport.

sections.title: Documentation and status
items: Added FORMAT.md MVP examples, editable boundaries, official sources and migration guidance; updated README, Agent guide and theme documentation.
Automated checks, browser observations and user acceptance are recorded separately. Source and static release packages use the same milestone commit; manual checks remain as documented.

v0_2_1.summary: library style entry points, CSS modules and local dependencies, with render snapshots and website Markdown-body adaptation.

sections.title: Library rendering
items: Libraries can declare CSS entries/modules with Tailwind layers, imports, nesting, fonts and local image/SVG assets. formatter configures virtual site-path mappings.
Added body containers, CSS viewports, display zoom, explicit heading anchors, node defaults and Prism code wrapping. Articles, themes, snippets and templates use isolated canvases.

Saving can record rendered output and immutable dependencies; history/Fork retain references. Existing records adopt a new environment only after explicit style updates; older manuscripts are not automatically migrated.
Added Markdown-body output. Document packages include required rendering dependencies; input, scrolling and unchanged candidate classes reuse compilation caches.

Website-body geometry at three viewports and existing WeChat flows were regression-tested. The static server supports local fonts/compression tasks; export child-window and preview-only output boundaries were fixed. General functionality has passed user acceptance.

v0_2_2.summary: Chinese/English UI, browser language preferences and bilingual documentation, implemented and audited one item at a time.

sections.title: Interface localization
items: Added i18next/react-i18next. Product dictionaries are organized by language and feature under locale/, with Chinese fallback, interpolation and plurals.
Language preferences live independently in the browser. Cold startup resolves language before showing the existing loading state; libraries and user content are not translated.
A language menu sits below the version, mutually exclusive with display mode. It reuses icons/tooltips/popovers, supports keyboard selection and preserves drafts/native undo.

Navigation, article lists, source toolbar, previews and find/replace use bilingual dictionaries. Product collection labels use IDs, user names/content remain unchanged, and language changes do not rebuild article canvases.
Theme, template, asset and settings pages use bilingual dictionaries. Filters, pagination, settings and actions retain IDs; library names, code and content remain original.

sections.title: Dialogs and product feedback
items: Dialogs, color/icon pickers, confirmations and disabled reasons use bilingual dictionaries; library names, code and custom-rule descriptions remain original.
Product diagnostics, statuses and errors retain stable message codes/parameters. Language changes update existing results, including source dots, provenance and line locations.
The static-start CLI shows Chinese/English help and errors according to system locale, retaining arguments, ports and exit behavior.
Restored sidebar display-mode padding, icons and compact menu sizing, with matching language controls; peer menus remain exclusive and keyboard-accessible.

sections.title: Release notes and localized display
items: Release notes retain original Chinese history and one source for version/status metadata, with separate English wording. Language changes preserve release/category expansion state.
Dates, months, counts, file sizes and zoom use UI-locale display formatting. Stored values, directories, sorting, filtering and form input remain unchanged.

sections.title: Bilingual documentation
items: Moved complete README, Agent, theme/snippet/template and format guides into zh-CN/en-US under docs/locale. The root README remains a bilingual entry; screenshots are shared through GitHub attachment URLs.

Updated language navigation, stable anchors, setup guidance and runtime repair-document paths. Complete examples in both languages are checked by production validators, configuration compilation and save/reload tests.

v0_2_2_1.summary: official dark-mode components, initialization templates, validation performance, drag-and-drop confirmation, preview scroll alignment and save behavior switches.

items.title: Official dark-mode integration
items: Included the article root in official dark conversion and prepared border and decorative paint inline. Original computed styles are captured before batch writes to an isolated copy, retaining declaration priority.

The official default template now uses the SDK's original text color and accepts an explicit library dark background. All 23 same-input Chrome comparisons passed; actual WeChat mobile output still needs checking.

items.title: Library algorithm components
items: Implementation and license load with each library and are checked file by file with SHA-256. Component IDs and JSON parameters are independent of workbench props; library switches, reloads and file changes update snapshot identity.

The official dark-mode adapter now lives in the public platform preset. Library code runs in an isolated sandbox; paint and findings are fully checked before application. Existing Blob images and fonts transfer in memory without scanning the whole library.

New render records retain the original algorithm code and license. Older libraries and records show a fallback when an algorithm is needed; damaged components, unknown capabilities and invalid results are never reported as passed.

items.title: New-library platform template
items: Library creation now offers a validation and processing template. WeChat Official Account is the only public option; its trio, algorithm code and license are initialized together. Unknown/private choices are rejected before directory selection, while cancellation and name-collision protections remain.
The default trio source now lives in resources/presets/platform/wechat-article/format. Private website preset directories are excluded from bundling.

items.title: Private platform configuration
items: Custom website libraries use independent format policies and CSS/resource dependencies without WeChat-specific limits or dark conversion. Private templates and dependencies remain local and are excluded from the public catalog and build.

items.title: Explicit platform validation switch
items: validator.meta.enabled can explicitly disable platform standards. The trio, algorithms and style dependencies still use shared loading and structural validation; product safety/resource checks remain and formatter behavior is independent. Missing or invalid configuration still fails; settings and reports show the state.

items.title: Library policy summary
items: Settings → Local directory now shows the active validation policy and algorithm version from the loaded snapshot. Switching libraries updates the summary; custom policies, fallbacks, disabled conversion and unavailable configurations are identified without extra library scans.

items.title: Confirm dropped images
items: The Assets page accepts external image drops and reuses the shared dialog shell to show destination, names, formats, sizes and unsupported entries before writing shared assets. Cancellation, library changes and stale targets do not import files; existing format, name-collision and partial-failure protections remain.

items.title: Writing and preview controls
items: Three shared icon switches in the preview header remember per-origin preferences: source-to-preview scrolling, manual-save format reports and save-only visible refresh.

Passive scrolling events are coalesced per frame using cached positions. Body, image, font or width changes invalidate the index, which rebuilds in bounded slices without library reads or compilation during scrolling.

Save reports default to on; disabling them only hides the manual-save dialog, while auto-save never opens it. Save-only refresh defaults to off; when enabled, visible inputs and resources are retained until successful saving. Current-draft checks, copying, export and render records stay independent, and stale display alignment pauses.

items.title: Source formatting shortcuts
items: Article source supports Cmd/Ctrl+B bold, I italic and U underline. Insert-menu hints share the same selection action, preserving chosen text instead of replacing it with sample text.
Actions reuse native single-step editing and input-specific undo history, with composition/read-only/unavailable guards. Markdown and HTML paragraph text use their corresponding inline markers.

items.title: Consistent editor theme controls
items: Confirmed the three Slate button fills are consumed. All built-in and Rainy editor themes now expose matching surface references while retaining existing colors. Every theme offers 33 base roles and 13 surface controls, including fields, shadows, backdrops, wash and opacity; editing a surface does not change its base color.

items.title: Expired rendition recovery
items: When the source or theme changes, an expired rendition is rebuilt after its retained dependencies are verified. Source files and historical styles are preserved; damaged dependencies still report an error rather than silently adopting current library styles.

items.title: Preview scroll recovery
items: Fixed wheel handling in fixed-viewport letterbox areas and stale drag state when changing split-view identity. Existing iframe scrolling is reused without changing the article virtual viewport.

items.title: Fast invalid-image diagnostics
items: Fixed repeated waits after an image had already failed with complete=true and naturalWidth=0. The engine handles settlement without reducing standards-JSON timeouts or requirements.

Empty/invalid addresses and loading/decoding failures are product resource errors for HTML/SVG images and local placeholders. Loading and resource-dependent incomplete states stay explicit; known missing files return diagnostics first.

items.title: Version opening and baseline
items: Opened from the 0.2.2 engineering work while retaining pending review. Algorithm, template, private configuration, performance and import work comes first, followed by preview scroll alignment, save-report and save-only refresh switches. The final audit covers only this patch and directly affected paths.

items.title: Static resource organization
items: Bundled fonts and OFL notices live in public/fonts, static licenses in public/licenses, and the sample image in public/images. Snippets/starters use the real /images/article-sample.png URL; old aliases and relative-image sample substitution are removed.

UI catalogs, release data and presets move into resources. Platform sources use resources/presets/platform; built-in themes/snippets/starters become files in resources/template/fresh-library. Browser scripts use public/format and public/algorithm, and initialization assembles the chosen public platform configuration.

items.title: Human review and follow-up fixes
items: Human review is closed for this release. Clipboard-receiver surfaces, shortcut spacing and combined save-only refresh/scroll alignment fixes are deferred to 0.3.0 and remain tracked as unresolved.

Broken images are reported by the full format check. Source-line regression checks and returning to unsaved editors with clear draft indicators continue in 0.3.0. Source saving remains separate from format results.

v0_3_0.summary: Read-only knowledge and Markdown/resource import with math/static diagrams, plus image zoom, folder renaming, WeChat copy fixes, global feedback and external complete fonts.

items.title: Read-only knowledge and relations
items: Each manuscript library can bind one independent read-only source. Indexes live in the manuscript library; explicit incremental/force scans, search, safe reading and link graphs retain missing/ambiguous/incomplete states.
Knowledge originals remain. Import editable copies with selected article themes; guards reject overlapping roots and stale writes.

items.title: Import and background tasks
items: Single UTF-8 Markdown creates body, theme snapshot and final references first. Local/HTTPS resources stream with bounded concurrency while editing, undo and save continue; arrivals never rewrite old full text.
Tasks offer pause/cancel/retry and source file/directory or replacement selection. Library switches/permission loss pause work; reopening requires manual recovery and conflicting files remain.

items.title: General assets and output
items: Image paths remain; attachments use media/file and shared/file. Twenty-three type icons, filtering, import confirmation, management and adoption share existing asset flows; non-images do not automatically preview or execute.

Checks distinguish importing/failed/missing resources and selective caches avoid rereading all images on arrival. Output rejects stale resource versions; ZIP carries explicit shared references with partial-output confirmation and excludes knowledge indexes/tasks.

items.title: Math and static diagrams
items: Optional markdown.math/markdown.mermaid steps produce local static MathML/isolated PNG. Older/default-disabled libraries keep behavior; invalid/oversized source is retained with diagnostics.

Trusted math commands and Mermaid config directives/interactions/external resources remain restricted. Pending diagrams cannot be copied/exported or saved as completed artifacts. Bilingual guides cover use, recovery, configuration, output and destination checks.

items.title: Article theme dark colors
items: Article color tables have light/dark columns. Library algorithm results are read only with multiple/unused/pending/failed states; one conversion supplies the entire table and preview.
Optional dark.tokens supplies manual overrides with light inheritance/reset. Variables apply before computed styles; fixed colors, old configurations/history and light output remain independent.

items.title: Bilingual library defaults
items: Complete Chinese and English themes, snippets, starter templates and categories share technical IDs and visual design. New libraries choose content from the interface language at creation.

The interface, missing translations and unsupported languages fall back to English; manual choice precedes browser languages. Libraries remember their seed language for initialization and Load defaults. Changing UI language leaves existing content untouched, and failed initialization retains its original choice.

Article themes share a library-level themes/preview.md sample for previews, save checks and color inspection. Missing files use the remembered seed language with an explicit default source; existing libraries and custom samples are not silently rewritten.

items.title: Manuscript folder renaming
items: Edit the article folder name in manuscript details. Applying it updates the index, project and ordering records, then reloads the manuscript. The information card and source header show the folder name; the body filename remains article.md.

items.title: External complete fonts
items: Complete Sen, Noto Sans SC and Roboto Mono fonts are excluded from the app and new builds, and still load from the library. Existing fonts and custom files are preserved.

Choose a font source in Settings before connecting a library: Google Fonts by default, or the free JSDMirror mirror for China. Missing files are checked for size and SHA-256 before writing. Failures fall back to system fonts, with cancellation, source switching and retry.
First-load guidance uses system fonts. README artwork shares the font source manifest and embeds verified complete fonts.

items.title: Width exemption and editor interaction
items: The horizontal-image snippet declares the official data-ignore-width exemption on its inner list. Outer width and other checks remain active; existing manuscripts are not rewritten.

Body findings from completed save, manual and output checks now appear in the source gutter. Editing or configuration changes invalidate old findings without adding layout checks during typing or scrolling.

items.title: History actions and layout
items: The restore action sits beside the source/render comparison tabs, using the shared button bar and history icon with the existing confirmation and checkpoint flow.
Wide layouts place article information and theme comparisons beside the history Fork form; narrow layouts stack them and retain access to long content.

items.title: Clipboard receiver paper
items: The receiver uses the current library’s light paper and text color across article preview modes. Native and button-based paste retain actual inline colors.

items.title: Formatting shortcut hints
items: B/I/U menu hints use spaced chords such as ⌘ B / Ctrl + B in both languages. Actual shortcuts, actions and keyboard semantics are unchanged.

items.title: Save-only refresh and scroll alignment
items: Alignment finds the visible ShadowRoot or iframe, combines with save-only refresh and rebinds after mode, width or document changes. Edited manuscripts retain their existing visible canvas when enabled; newly opened documents wait for their own styles.

Retained displays map saved source to the current draft. Edited gaps use the nearest valid node; no match retains the current position. Warm scrolling reads cached positions, with passive events, requestAnimationFrame and 4 ms rebuild slices.
The top retention notice is removed. Save-only mode adds “· Save to refresh preview” to the source footer’s saved state.

items.title: Unsaved drafts and return to editing
items: Continue editing returns to the protected manuscript, information dialog, theme, snippet, starter template, appearance or asset editing position. Close and Escape only dismiss the prompt; failed saves retain the draft.

Navigation and object entries reuse unsaved dots, while article rows add a danger-colored Unsaved tag. Saving, discarding or undoing back to saved content clears the mark. Filters and background tasks are not unsaved edits.

items.title: Scrollable containers and updated snippets
items: Clarified the existing vertical-scroll height exemption. Both built-in languages now have 21 snippets, including four-image rows with and without padding. Width exemption stays on the inner list; SVG click behavior remains frozen.

items.title: Image viewing and zoom
items: The local article image view-and-rename dialog shows full images within the available width and supports vertical scrolling. Rename controls remain reachable in short windows; the separate image preview retains zoom and navigation.
Image viewers support Ctrl/⌘ + wheel zoom. Centered controls at the bottom zoom in, zoom out, or fit the width; ordinary wheel scrolling still moves through long images.

items.title: Manuscript details layout
items: The folder heading sits above the path card in manuscript details, with combined guidance for applying folder changes and saving the article. Narrow screens retain a scrolling form and bottom actions.

items.title: Global action feedback
items: Folder rename results appear below the toolbar as global notifications. Success says only “Folder updated”; manuscript details no longer retain a result row.

Success notifications disappear after three seconds. Errors and warnings retain details and can be dismissed. New results replace earlier ones for the same operation, with at most two visible; dialog keyboard and focus behavior is preserved.

items.title: Caret and preview switching
items: Fixed source clicks jumping to the old caret after saving or replacement. Typing // or opening the snippet picker closes find while retaining its form values.

Save-only refresh identifies previews by library, month, manuscript directory and opening generation, fixing the previous manuscript's canvas remaining after switching articles. Unsaved edits within one manuscript still keep its saved preview.

items.title: Older render record compatibility
items: Fixed older render records being rejected after adding the dark-source field. Existing manuscripts and history retain their original configuration without bulk migration; body, theme and dependency checks remain active.

items.title: Folder punctuation preservation
items: Folder names preserve valid Chinese and full-width punctuation through saving and reopening. Path separators, reserved characters and collision checks remain protected.

items.title: Quote copying and preview shells
items: WeChat rich-text copying outputs quotes as section elements while retaining their theme styles. Source and preview continue to use blockquote.

Copied content no longer includes preview-shell page padding, centering or width/height constraints. Spacing inside content cards, paragraphs and quotes is preserved. The library formatter controls these policies; older configurations retain their existing behavior until explicitly updated.

items.title: Dark-preview borders and background hierarchy
items: Fixed inline borders containing CSS variables losing their width and style when dark-mode colors were applied. Each side retains its original geometry, written only to the isolated copy after result validation.

Aligned the outer quote surface in Rainy Design with the Basic theme to restore background hierarchy after the official dark-mode conversion. The official algorithm, manuscript source and historical theme snapshots remain unchanged.

items.title: Refresh after adopting an article theme
items: Adopting or updating an article theme immediately recompiles styles and refreshes the current preview after success, including one explicit refresh in save-only mode. Subsequent typing still follows that preference. Unsaved state is preserved; failed or superseded compilation never advances the preview. Copy and export use valid results for the current theme.

items.title: Version and MVP scope
items: Continues from the 0.2.2.1 engineering branch with earlier review records and native-browser gaps preserved. Read-only binding, indexing/search/graph, import/resources and math/Mermaid are implemented, audited and committed one item at a time without releasing.

items.title: Release-log separation and responsive configuration
items: Public release data moved to resources/changelog/public.json. Local development and review notes use resources/changelog/local.md, excluded from Git and public exports; historical notices and bilingual pairs remain intact.

Documentation examples use viewport:null to lay out at the actual preview-column width and scroll within the available height. Explicit viewport objects remain available for fixed-layout reproduction.

v0_3_0_1.summary: Clarify preview refresh after theme adoption, save-only behavior, configuration reloading and saving boundaries.

sections.title: Documentation corrections
items: Synchronize the English and Chinese README, theme, format and Agent guides: successfully adopting a different or updated theme refreshes the preview once; subsequent body edits still follow the save-only preference.

Clarify that theme adoption adds no save operation, external format JSON edits still require reopening the library and explicitly updating styles, and failed or stale compilation does not advance the preview.

v0_3_1.summary: Library capabilities, theme-save policy and renderer modularization; refined history, themed search, long-document gutters, statistics and image previews, with synchronized theme/snippet defaults.

sections.title: New features
items: An optional config.json and trio metadata declare stylesheet authority, preview mode and operation capabilities. Theme sample resource failures can remain reviewable while the library policy permits saving.
History actions are grouped at the top. Metadata and Fork use child dialogs; manual deletion confirms one version, while protection continues to restrict automatic cleanup.

Document rendering, style compilation, isolated canvases and output conversion live in article-format. Legacy entries forward to the same implementation; workspace workflows and stored library/history protocols are retained.

sections.title: Experience improvements
items: Editor themes have independent light/dark search highlights, defaulting to fluorescent yellow. Find floats over the source with entry/exit transitions; matches center in the source viewport, and Cmd/Ctrl+F from the preview opens that same find panel.

Source numbers match the complete file, including a collapsible read-only metadata view. Body diagnostics use file coordinates; the gutter expands without wrapping, and files over 1000 lines suggest refreshing the preview only after saving.
Theme and snippet defaults reflect the current wechat edits, including Rainy Design 1.0.58. Localized seed wording is retained and existing article theme snapshots are not migrated.
Metadata and body share line-number gutters and text insets. A -3px offset places the full 2px button outline inside the edge to prevent clipping.

History reuses the editor header with information/Fork icon actions. Source/layout switches beside the date, with a fading light/dark switch for both layout previews. Protected versions keep a lock icon; unprotected actions appear on card hover or focus. Directory/snapshot context joins the status line.

sections.title: Fixes
items: Statistics recognize standard and website document containers through common body markers, exclude preview decoration and retain readiness/configuration guards.
Loaded images in normal, library and dark-copy previews open the shared zoom dialog. Static copies retain click handling, and preview interaction attributes are excluded from copied body content.

v0_3_1_1.summary: Fix library startup failure recovery, live preview and sidebar selector spacing, and align README release badges.

sections.title: Experience improvements
items: Keep the visible preview container and reading position while merging consecutive edits; reduce unnecessary background conversions in save-only mode.
Restore internal spacing in sidebar appearance and language selectors while preserving light/dark styling and keyboard focus.
Show the Release badge alongside License and dependency badges in READMEs, linked to the current release.

sections.title: Bug fixes
items: Finish the format loading state when library initialization or reading fails, so the workspace does not wait indefinitely.

v0_3_2.summary: Multiple knowledge sources and a lightweight writing-reference panel support search, excerpts, free-text citations, topics and source-change review. Library render packages, source CSS editing, original-source recovery and webpage output are refined alongside editing, assets and history.

sections.title: Libraries and render packages
items: Each library can maintain rendering, validation and settings in its own format package and declare formatting, copying and export actions.
Existing manuscripts and history retain their render records, interpreter and resources. Explicitly Update styles to adopt the current library environment; no automatic migration.
Stronger consistency checks across manuscript text, configuration and image resources prevent stale rendering or output after changes.
New libraries offer an Empty validator preset while retaining general syntax, resource and safety checks. Configuration synchronization preserves user modifications.
Resource previews share default/available host width without changing internal viewport, content-owned widths or manuscript exports.
Current successful preview CSS has a read-only viewer with mode/configuration identity. Library-owned styles retain theme CSS originals; unused-color text follows the existing swatch popup content.

The empty preset starts in the selected language with no snippets or snippet categories and three plain-Markdown starters. Reopening preserves cleared content; explicitly loading defaults retains the original seed choice and user edits. The WeChat preset keeps its existing resources.

The theme editor edits declared source CSS and reloads under the current SHA policy; disabling verification preserves configuration bytes. Theme CSS, generated output and saved snapshots remain separate, with conflicts and partial writes reported distinctly.

New libraries use rainy-format/2 with library-root paths, deep styles directories and JSON resource aliases. Legacy protocols and history remain intact; upgrades are explicit, with algorithm code and notices maintained through versioned manifests.

Expected SHA verification is configurable and enabled by default. Explicitly disabling it permits IDE edits and read-only reload; synchronize expected hashes before re-enabling. Actual file identity, conflicts and history protection remain.
The host guarantees complete Markdown-source download, including metadata and unsaved edits, even when configuration or rendering fails. This is separate from body-only export.
Webpage output can embed declared local styles and resources, resolving library aliases and temporary resource URLs. External HTTPS resources remain subject to permissions and network availability.

sections.title: Knowledge and research materials
items: A manuscript library can connect multiple external knowledge sources, each with its own index and research data. External originals remain read-only.
Search supports same-paragraph ranking, grouped passages, exact phrases, exclusions, and title and path filters.
Safe reading supports contents, source locations, document links and anchors, with a return to previous reading positions.
Create independent topics, link manuscripts and collect full documents or passages while retaining notes, order and captured text.
Existing inbound and outbound links show their source sentences and locations, with navigation to related documents and the graph.
Review changes to collected sources centrally, adjust locations and explicitly decide whether to update retained snapshots. Manuscript text stays unchanged.
Knowledge-source actions move to the top page toolbar. View tabs, reading actions and pagination use icons and tooltips.
Refine the two collapsible source and document rails with persistent icons and tooltips, corrected card spacing, ellipses for collapsed empty states and theme-aware loading progress.
All five knowledge views share the top toolbar. Search filters gain icons and spacing; Toast feedback and a fixed diagnostics entry preserve reading height.

The graph starts in Local mode with two hops. Switches control scope/depth and icon actions control zoom, reset, location, reading and center. Help retains its display policy; clipping notices stay locked while the condition persists and become dismissible after it clears.

The reading toolbar separates line numbers, article creation, download, passage collection and whole-document collection. Passages require a valid selection, contents stay open after navigation, and line numbers follow the original source without changing its text.

Collections, references and changes share responsive research cards. Captured text is immediately visible; upper and lower reference regions open the source sentence and target. Notes, order and explicit snapshot review are preserved.

Fix knowledge collection eligibility for the active selection and topic while preserving both controls and their labels. Rename manuscript creation to “Create article” and prevent grouped search results from clipping.
Place shelf topic notes and linked manuscripts in a separate information panel; open captured content and notes from a card's preview or title.
Move or copy shelf captures between topics in the same source, open originals or remove captures; replace up/down controls with manual drag order and six automatic sort orders.

sections.title: Writing references and citations
items: The editor gains a dedicated lightweight reference panel above the manuscript preview. Collapse it or drag the divider to adjust the two regions.
Browse sources and responsive document cards, then open full read-only previews. Breadcrumb navigation preserves the previous selection and scroll position.
The excerpt action becomes available for a valid selection in the current reference, adopts exactly the selected text and preserves the manuscript insertion position.
Add free-text citations to existing arguments while retaining the manuscript selection and appending the marker after it. Source details are optional.
Explicitly reuse citation numbers, edit in a dialog or at the manuscript end, and manually renumber or remove unused entries. Legacy citations require explicit adoption; code examples stay unchanged.
Add icons to Renumber, Save entry text and Insert citation while preserving their order, tooltips and disabled states.

sections.title: Editing and history
items: Auto-save and automatic snapshots pause outside the editor and resume according to existing settings. Auto-save defaults to off for new libraries; explicit preferences are preserved.
Correct source line-number alignment after soft wrapping. The metadata disclosure spans the source column, with separately scrolling expanded content.
In Replace, Enter replaces the current match and Cmd/Ctrl+Enter confirms Replace all. Tooltips show the shortcuts, and Replace all remains a single undoable edit.
Source and reference text share a thin-scrollbar viewport with transparent tracks, editor-theme colors and consistent gutter space. Reference text also aligns with its header.
Center the column-divider handle, remove the duplicate saved indicator from the preview toolbar and move its light/dark switch to the left of the three preview buttons.
Refine the history title, version details, comparison switch and top actions. Forking a historical version reports its result promptly and restores focus correctly.
Fix false centering warnings during normal image scaling while retaining checks for actual alignment changes and overflow.

Selection menus share hierarchical navigation, space-aware presentation and keyboard controls. Asset types are grouped by category, selections inside dialogs preserve focus, and child-option icons align with their parent directory text, with an SVG selection mark at the trailing edge.

The folder name in manuscript details is saved with Save article. Remove the separate apply action, duplicate saved badge and rename-success notification while retaining name-collision, unsaved-change and failure protections.

sections.title: Assets and snippets
items: Add individual transfer actions to asset cards and details, and support Escape to exit selection mode.

Cards and details show consistent reference status. Resources referenced by manuscripts, history or shared locations are copied; unreferenced resources are moved. Unknown states restrict actions, and execution rechecks references.
Snippets gain category creation and duplication actions. Copies are edited independently with source code, description, icon and category retained, while names and triggers are checked for conflicts.

Mac-style code-window snippets offer wrapping and non-wrapping variants, synchronized with bilingual built-in resources and authorized libraries. They use utility classes and preserve existing manuscripts and historical snapshots.

sections.title: Data protection and recovery
items: Relocating a knowledge source preserves its identity, topics and citation links. Replacing it requires separate confirmation, and deletion or replacement retains the old research partition.
Manuscript or directory renames retain existing topic and citation associations so path changes do not lose research links.
Failed first auxiliary-data writes clean up only verified residues from that operation and allow retry, preserving existing and externally changed content.

sections.title: Page layout and feedback
items: Article lists add six sort orders and place tag filters beside the list heading. Import actions gain icons; refresh becomes an icon button. Sorting preserves sidebar organization. Row numbers share the header selection button’s centerline and remain centered for three-digit values.
The history light/dark switch stays visible and is unavailable in source comparison, with an explanatory tooltip. Returning to rendered comparison preserves the previous choice.

Article assets gain collapsible project navigation. Cards, details and selection mode share consistent action order and support selected downloads while retaining reference checks and copy/move boundaries.

Necessary explicit-operation results appear directly in Toasts, with information buttons only for extra content. Startup neither produces, queues nor replays ordinary notices; blocking failures show causes and recovery centrally. Refresh restoration and successful background saves/snapshots stay quiet. Button progress, typing and ordinary previews do not announce again; manual library loading gives one aggregate result.

Toast success, warning and error tones follow operation results. An information icon after the main text opens details with 500ms size and text-opacity transitions; expanded reading and keyboard focus pause the remaining auto-dismiss timer. Auto-dismiss notices show a counterclockwise countdown ring around the close icon; hovering anywhere on the notice pauses the remaining time.
Empty operation entries are hidden; unavailable business actions retain their reason. Article-list Fork results use Toast feedback, while CSS inspection and theme/version details remain available.
Remove duplicate footer Close actions from captured-content and read-only CSS dialogs. Prevent a stationary pointer from overriding keyboard selection while the snippet list scrolls.

Toasts share states, actions and automatic/manual/locked lifetimes. Three remain visible by default and extra notices queue. Global positioning uses top-12; Tailwind state styles control entry/exit direction and opacity. Measured layout motion, page persistence and counterclockwise rings remain, while reading and async actions pause the shared clock.

Preview controls occupy their header or an external toolbar, allowing long labels and narrow layouts to wrap. Configuration problems share the Validation and algorithms header; reload results announce directly, separately from instructions.

The main navigation and article sidebar each remember their desktop expanded or collapsed state across refresh. Unavailable browser storage retains session choices; temporary mobile drawers are not persisted.
Library action dialogs add shared icons to Cancel and Download; the action button is labeled Download.
The shared CSS editor uses remaining height with reachable bottom actions and a dismissible impact notice; narrow layouts retain independent scrolling.

sections.title: Agent guides and online access
items: Root and bilingual READMEs add online access, explain local-directory permission and distinguish the online release from development versions.

Bilingual guides cover controllable desktop-browser prerequisites, new/existing library checkpoints, step-by-step or direct use, and four artifact-based tutorials with save/reopen checks. Public Agent entry guidance remains separate from maintainer governance.

Finalized Toast, trash and editor-refresh behavior is documented with bilingual record contracts. Paired example assets save/reload on isolated disk libraries; Chrome replay covers writing, appearance adoption, combined previews/rich-text receiving and importing/editing a preserved original.
Revise bilingual manuals: README focuses on use, THEME/FORMAT retain authoring contracts, and AGENT-GUIDE adds cold-start task routing, contract identification, failure recovery and delivery checks.

sections.title: Article recovery and refresh
items: Article trash defaults to enabled, retaining the complete body, theme, assets, history and recovery metadata in _trash/. Normal deletion offers ten-second Undo and later restoration from the sidebar trash entry without overwriting occupied paths.

Settings has three workflow cards with matching switches. Disabled controls retain values. With trash disabled, explicit permanent deletion has no Undo; existing trash remains restorable and invalid settings block deletion. The cards align at their bottom edges, with the trash path and clear action on one row. Save settings and appearance actions align with the bottom of their heading descriptions.

Clearing a fixed batch offers thirty-second Undo before physical cleanup; notices and receipts share the remaining clock. Closing a notice or navigating never commits early; refresh/reopen resumes checked records, while later entries stay outside the earlier batch.

Refreshing the editor reopens this tab’s saved article in the same library. Other pages stay in place, invalid identities return to the list with feedback, and active navigation cancels a late restore. Unsaved body text is not persisted.

v0_3_2_1.summary: Fixes subpath render assets and article-save record timing; simplifies feedback, unifies title editing and load recovery, and updates themes and snippets.

sections.title: Fixes and usability
items: Host sandboxes, previews and scripts support an explicit deployment prefix while retaining isolation, cancellation and timeout protection.
Article saving completes folder handling, rendering and record persistence in one flow, reporting complete or partial results without rolling back saved source.
Operation notices use concise headings with paths and failure causes in additional details; redundant transitional messages are removed.
Article titles share an editable component; titles and folders size to content within their containers. Load failures retain the centered message and recovery actions, with icons using theme colors.

Syncs Rainy theme 1.0.61, chapter and H3 snippets, callout opacity and a new chapter style; both code snippets follow the finalized wechat library source while preserving existing libraries and historical snapshots.
Cleans up obsolete and duplicate bilingual messages and adds key, parameter and historical-record compatibility checks, preserving existing notice wording and library records.
Corrects the default code snippets to match the finalized library sources. Please download the packages again if you obtained an earlier copy.
